hook: One line in a lead form decides whether your sales team talks to buyers, or to browsers. Most forms ask for name, phone, email. That tells you nothing about whether the person can actually buy what you sell.
body:
One line in a lead form decides whether your sales team talks to buyers, or to browsers.

Most forms ask for name, phone, email. That tells you nothing about whether the person can actually buy what you sell.

A Tirupur apparel manufacturer ran a campaign where the ad and the form both stated a 200-piece minimum order, up front. 19 wholesale buyers responded, at under $6 an enquiry.

Compare that to the same manufacturer's wider lead campaigns: 4,248 leads at ₹16.58 each across six campaigns. Cheaper leads, no qualifying question in front of them.

Neither number is wrong. They are two different products. Cheap leads fill a sheet. Qualified leads fill a sales call.

The qualifying question is not about your product. It is about the one thing that would make someone unable to buy from you at all — minimum order size, budget, location, timeline. Put that one thing in the form, in plain words, before you ask for a phone number.

You will get fewer leads. You will also stop handing your sales team people who were never going to say yes.

slides.text: One lead form question decides who your sales team actually talks to.
Cheap leads and leads that close are two different products, not one.
Most forms ask name, phone, email — nothing that rules anyone out.

slides.label: LEADS AT ₹16.58
slides.text: A Tirupur manufacturer got 4,248 wholesale leads at ₹16.58 each, no qualifying question in front of them.

slides.left: Form asks name, phone, email only
slides.right: Form states the one thing that rules someone out
slides.text: Same ad budget, two different questions in the form.

slides.label: AT UNDER $6 EACH
slides.text: The same manufacturer ran a campaign where the ad and form both stated a 200-piece minimum.
19 buyers responded to that minimum, at under $6 an enquiry — fewer leads, one condition stated upfront.
Pick your one qualifier before you touch the ad.
items: Find the single fact that rules someone out — order size, budget, location, timeline
State it plainly in the ad and again in the form
Never bury it as a dropdown with 'other' as an option

slides.label: THE TRADE
slides.text: A qualifier costs you volume. It buys back your sales team's time.
The hook holds: one honest question in a form changes who shows up on the other side of it.
Write the one fact that would make someone wrong for you. Put it in the form before you ask for their number.
